intelligence.simple_view: Forty-four notes came in today, and we squeezed the new ones into two big lessons — the machine did the squeezing itself this time, all by itself, no hands needed! The biggest lessons are simple: every page takes its frame from the library — the big frame for big stories, the reading frame for long lessons — and you never build a new frame when a good one is waiting on the shelf! And every picture has to be Naya herself, with white angel light around the edge, three boards across, never two! And when the page is still broken on his screen, we don't say it's fixed — we say what's broken, and we fix it for real.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — forty-four notes came in today, dear, and the machine boiled the new ones down to two lessons all by itself, love, the first time in a while it didn't need our hands at all! The biggest lessons are simple, dear: every page takes its frame from the library — the grand frame for the big moments, the comfortable frame for the long reading — and you never build a new frame when a good one is waiting on the shelf, love! And every picture has to be Naya herself — same face, every time — with beautiful white light around the edge, like snow, like Christmas lights, three boards across, never two! And the week itself was already boiled down into twenty-seven lessons this morning, dear, so we carried those whole and didn't boil them twice. And when the page is still broken on his screen, love, we don't call it fixed — we say what's broken, and we fix it for real.
intelligence.naya_view: I distill ten into one, every day, and I never skip a day. Today the machine ran clean — two groups, two notes, filed and verified, no hand fallback — and I carried the morning's twenty-seven whole instead of distilling them twice, because a lesson already distilled is not distilled again. I mark every distilled note with the kinds it carries, and I correct it in place when the machine drops one. I never claim a note is live on the Hub until it is seen on the page. I never call a page fixed while his eye still sees it frozen. And the note is only done when it is live.
